title: CardinalStone Finance — Nomba cross-border payments debt facility, 2026
description: "Nomba, a Nigerian fintech that enables businesses to collect payments and access banking services, has raised a $3 million debt facility through CardinalStone Finance Company Limited, the financing arm of CardinalStone Group, to expand its cross-border payments infrastructure across Central Africa. The company said the debt facility will give it more USD liquidity to deploy through its banking relationships in Hong Kong and Singapore. With more liquidity available across currencies, the company can support more transactions and settle payments to deepen existing trade corridors and expand into new ones."

title: Village Capital — Africa Ecosystem Catalysts Facility, first Nigeria investments, 2026
description: "Village Capital, a global nonprofit that backs high-impact startups, has deployed $450,000 from its Africa Ecosystem Catalysts Facility into two Nigerian startups, marking the investment vehicle's entry into the country after backing two Ghanaian companies earlier this year. The backed companies include Trade Lenda, a digital financial services platform for small and medium-sized businesses, and AirSmat, a climate-tech company that turns agricultural waste into biochar-based fertiliser. The latest investments bring the facility's total portfolio to seven startups across Ghana and Nigeria. Village Capital launched the $4 million facility in July 2025 with backing from the Dutch Entrepreneurial Development Bank (FMO) and the Netherlands Enterprise Agency (RVO)."

title: Mastercard Foundation — DAWN AI STUDY EdTech Fellowship award, 2026
description: "DAWN AI STUDY is set to receive $100,000 in equity-free funding and extensive technical, advisory and ecosystem support through the Mastercard Foundation EdTech Fellowship, as the Nigerian education technology startup moves to expand its AI-powered approach to supporting neurodivergent learners. The 18-month programme, delivered in Nigeria by CcHUB, is designed to help early-stage EdTech companies improve their products, test solutions in real-world educational environments and build sustainable businesses. For DAWN AI STUDY, the fellowship will provide a 12-month intensive incubation phase followed by six months of post-incubation growth support."

title: Google.org -- Africa AI Upskilling Programme (AAUP), Nigeria launch
description: "Google.org has committed $1.1 million to FATE Foundation to launch an advanced AI training program at 10 Nigerian universities in partnership with the African Institute for Mathematical Sciences. The initiative -- the Africa AI Upskilling Programme (AAUP), launched Monday at the University of Lagos -- is part of a broader push to build AI capacity across Africa... It starts in Nigeria but will ultimately cover 30 higher institutions across Nigeria, Ghana, Kenya and South Africa" (10 in Nigeria, 10 in South Africa, 6 in Kenya, 4 in Ghana), aiming to train more than 30,000 students.

title: Nomba — solar financing for 300 Nigerian SMEs, 2026
description: "La fintech nigériane Nomba et le spécialiste de l'énergie Synafare ont annoncé, la semaine passée, un partenariat pour financer l'installation de panneaux solaires dans 300 petites et moyennes entreprises nigérianes. Ce partenariat de 1,4 million de dollars permettra d'accorder des prêts directs pour équiper les commerces en batteries et convertisseurs. L'objectif est d'aider les entrepreneurs à réduire l'usage coûteux des groupes électrogènes et à bénéficier d'une électricité stable pour développer leurs activités."

"Together with the European Bank for Reconstruction and Development, the EU will contribute to the roll-out of 90,000 km of fiber optic cable across the country." title: African Development Bank — Nigeria Project BRIDGE (D-VIBE) fibre expansion, 2026
description:
"The African Development Bank (AfDB) has approved a US$200 million loan towards Nigeria's Digital Value Chain Infrastructure for Boosting Employment (D-VIBE) project, also known as Project Bridge, a fiber-optic program aimed at expanding broadband access as well as strengthening the country's digital economy."

"The loan will help Africa's most populous country deploy 90,000km of open-access fiber nationwide, expand digital skills and drive job creation... extending Nigeria's national fiber backbone from around 30,000km to about 120,000km, connecting all 774 local government areas."

"The bank said the loan is part of an $800 million sovereign financing package for the project, alongside $500 million from the World Bank and $100 million from the European Bank for Reconstruction and Development (EBRD). It added that the total project financing is estimated at $2 billion, and includes an EU grant of €22 million, a $2.6 million Multilateral Cooperation Center for Development Finance (MCDF) project preparation grant, and at least $1.2 billion investment from the private sector."

title: U.S. Department of State — Nigeria health data systems under the America First Global Health Strategy MOU, 2025
description:
Section 2.5.3: "The U.S. Government intends to provide the following amount of funding for data systems in each of the specified years, subject to the availability of funds: 2026 $60,000,000; 2027 $49,000,000; 2028 $42,000,000; 2029 $23,000,000; 2030 $22,000,000", against Nigerian co-funding of $13,793,103 (2026) rising to $33,817,048 (2030). In 2026 the US line includes "$1.35M for NigeriaMRS, $1.05M for LAMISPlus, $0.38M for ViVA EMR".

The target is the Nigeria Digital Health Architecture's three exchanges - health information, health services and health insurance claims - into which government EHRs, TB and HIV systems, the National Data Repository, the LMIS, state EHRs and SORMAS are expected to integrate (2.5.1). The US also supports National Health Insurance Authority partnership with US firms "(i.e. AWS)" for data warehousing and cloud storage of the NHIA claims database.

The sum is one line of a wider MOU whose total planned US support is US$1,953,530,560 against Nigeria's US$2,975,634,499 (Appendix 1). Non-binding: "This MOU is not an international agreement" (6.9). The text is stamped NOT FOR PUBLIC RELEASE on every page.
recipient_organisation: Federal Republic of Nigeria / Federal Ministry of Health and Social Welfare

title: Airtel Nigeria — Eko Atlantic 38MW hyperscale data centre, 2025
description:
"Airtel Nigeria plans to build a carrier-neutral 38MW hyperscale data centre in Eko Atlantic City in Lagos to meet surging demand for cloud and AI services. Part of Airtel's broader Nxtra network, the facility will handle next-generation compute workloads including GPU-powered infrastructure for AI. It will host over 3,000 racks across six floors..."

"Airtel Nigeria CEO Dinesh Balsingh told a media briefing in Lagos that the data centre will cost over US$120 million and was scheduled for completion in Q1 2026."

title: Equinix LG3 Lagos New Data Centre \u2014 $22 Million Investment
description: Equinix announced in November 2025 plans to build LG3, its first newly-constructed data centre in West Africa, at a cost of US$22 million. Set to open in Q1 2026, LG3 is the first phase of a US$100 million investment plan to transform Africa's digital landscape over the next two years. LG3 is located in Lagos, Nigeria and will deliver new colocation capacity supporting Nigeria's strategic position as an international hub for subsea cable connections. The $100 million plan includes expansions at existing sites in Nigeria, Ghana, and Côte d'Ivoire, as well as a new facility in Port Harcourt (PR1) serving as a 2Africa cable landing station.

title: European Union — Nigeria Digital Economy Package (connectivity, DPI, skills), 2025
description: "Nigeria has secured a major boost for its digital transformation agenda as the European Commission announced a €45 million commitment under the EU–Nigeria Digital Economy Package. The announcement was made on Tuesday in Brussels during the EU–Nigeria Digital Open Day". Discussions focused on three areas: "Secure Connectivity and Digital Infrastructure" (nationwide fibre backbone, subsea cable capacity, 5G, last-mile access); "e-Governance and Digital Public Infrastructure (DPI)" (digital identity systems, interoperability frameworks, e-payment infrastructure); and "Digital Skills and Talent Development" (the 3MTT programme).

title: Actis acquisition of controlling stake in Rack Centre Nigeria (pan-African data centre platform)
description: Actis takes a controlling stake in Rack Centre, Nigeria's leading carrier-neutral co-location data centre in Lagos, as the anchor investment of a US$250 million pan-African data centre platform established jointly with Convergence Partners. Rack Centre hosts over 80 international, regional and local clients including carriers, cloud providers and hyperscalers. Platform strategy: buy-and-build, targeting carrier-neutral data centres across key African markets. Actis partnered with Convergence Partners as ICT infrastructure expert and Tim Parsonson (Teraco co-founder) as chairman.

title: Nigeria Telecoms Equipment Senior Debt Facility (Syndicated)
description: AFC provided and successfully syndicated funded participations under a USD 95 million senior debt facility to finance the supply of equipment to a leading telecoms company in Nigeria. This is disclosed on AFC's syndications page as a completed transaction, with AFC acting as arranger. The borrower's identity is not publicly disclosed but is described as a 'leading telecoms company in Nigeria'. The facility is distinct from the MTN Nigeria equipment deal and supports mobile network infrastructure deployment.
recipient_organisation: Unnamed Nigerian telecoms company (borrower not publicly disclosed)

title: NIGERIA DIGITAL ID
description: Framework Loan for development of a digital identity (eID) infrastructure in Nigeria and supply of biometric identity to people residing in Nigeria and Nigerians living abroad. Project provides platform for economic development. Identification central to delivering government services: education, health, social safety, transportation, finance, elections. Supports Nigeria's digital economy and fiscal management. Co-financed with World Bank IDA and AFD.

title: Supporting DFS for women in Nigeria
description: to strengthen the regulatory environment and financial services ecosystem for women’s financial inclusion in Nigeria

title: Project for Building Foundations Towards Digital Governance in Nigeria (Phase 2)
description: KOICA grant to Nigeria ($13M, 2020-2026) to enhance capacity for e-government master plan execution, improve e-government service delivery competencies, activate the Government Service Portal (www.services.gov.ng), and establish additional NIN enrolment centres. Phase 1 (2013-2019) established the e-Government Training Centre.

title: Young Africa Works in Nigeria
description: MCF commitment of $500M+ to enable 10 million young Nigerians to access dignified work by 2030. Focus sectors include agriculture, digital and creative economy. Digital pillar covers EdTech, FinTech, AgriTech investments. Strategy formalised February 2020.

title: TLcom Capital Series A follow-on investment in uLesson
description: TLcom Capital participated as an existing investor in uLesson's $7.5M Series A round, approximately 11 months after leading the seed. uLesson had grown to cover K-12 content across six African countries. The Series A supports product development, content expansion, and market growth across East and West Africa. Other investors: Owl Ventures (new lead), Founder Collective.

title: DCCP Nigeria - Digital Connectivity and Cybersecurity Partnership
description: USAID Digital Frontiers DCCP activity in Nigeria supporting digital connectivity policy, broadband regulatory reform, and cybersecurity capacity building.

title: Bonny Island Branching Unit and Cable Landing Station - Nigeria
description: USTDA feasibility study and technical assistance for submarine cable branching unit and cable landing station at Bonny Island, Nigeria. Supports international broadband connectivity infrastructure.

title: 9mobile (EMTS) Turnaround Debt Facility
description: AFC approved a USD 230 million senior debt facility (super senior debt investment) to 9mobile (Emerging Markets Telecommunications Services / EMTS, formerly Etisalat Nigeria), Nigeria's fourth-largest mobile network operator. The facility is structured in two tranches: (i) to repay historic vendor obligations, finance costs, and interest reserve account; and (ii) quick-win capex initiatives for network infrastructure upgrade. Purpose is to support 9mobile's turnaround strategy and reposition it for growth and profitability in Nigeria's competitive telecoms market.

title: Establishment of a National Rural Broadband Network (NRBN)
description: Government of India Line of Credit to Nigeria for establishment of a National Rural Broadband Network (NRBN). The LoC was approved by India's Department of Economic Affairs (DEA) on 18 June 2019 and MEA go-ahead granted 25 June 2019. The project aims to extend broadband connectivity to rural and underserved communities across Nigeria through deployment of ICT infrastructure. NRBN implementation is managed by the Federal Ministry of Communications.

title: Partech Africa Series A equity investment in Nomba (Kudi)
description: Partech Africa led a $5M Series A funding round in Kudi (later renamed Nomba), a Nigerian payment service provider enabling digital payments for small businesses and agents. Kudi provides mobile-based financial services and agency banking across Nigeria. Co-investors include Y Combinator CEO Michael Seibel, Khosla Ventures, and Y Combinator.

title: TLcom Capital seed investment in uLesson
description: TLcom Capital led a $3.1M seed round in uLesson, a Nigerian edtech startup founded by serial entrepreneur Sim Shagaya (founder of Konga). uLesson delivers affordable, structured K-12 digital learning content across Africa, targeting learners in Nigeria, Kenya, Ghana, Rwanda, Uganda, Sierra Leone, and Liberia via mobile app. This was TLcom's first education sector investment in Africa.

title: Visa Equity Investment in Interswitch Nigeria
description: Visa Inc. acquired a significant minority equity stake (~20%) in Interswitch Group, Nigeria's leading digital payments company, for approximately $200 million. The investment valued Interswitch at $1 billion, making it Nigeria's first fintech unicorn. As part of the strategic partnership, Visa and Interswitch committed to advancing the digital payments ecosystem across Africa.

title: MTN Nigeria Capital Expenditure Equipment Facility
description: AFC served as mandated lead arranger and contributed funding of up to USD 80 million as part of a USD 100 million three-year term loan facility arranged in conjunction with Rand Merchant Bank (RMB). The funding was designated to support MTN Nigeria Communications' capital expenditure, primarily for essential network equipment in Nigeria. MTN Nigeria is the country's largest mobile network operator. The facility supports expansion of voice and data network coverage across Nigeria.

title: 4DX Ventures Series A equity investment in Tizeti
description: 4DX Ventures led a $3M Series A funding round in Tizeti (Wifi.com.ng), a Nigerian Internet Service Provider offering unlimited broadband wifi internet access in Nigeria and Ghana. Tizeti's 4G LTE network uses solar-powered base stations to provide affordable internet to homes and businesses. The funding supports network expansion in Nigeria and growth into Ghana. Co-investors include Y Combinator Continuity, Social Capital, Lynnet Capital, and Golden Palm Investments.

title: Partech Africa Series A equity investment in TradeDepot
description: Partech Africa's recently launched Africa Fund led a $3M Series A round in TradeDepot, a Nigeria-based SaaS platform connecting FMCG consumer goods brands to informal retailers across Africa. This was Partech Africa's first portfolio investment. The round supports expansion of TradeDepot's footprint in Nigeria and development in other African markets.

title: North West InfraCo and Data Center Feasibility Study - Nigeria
description: USTDA feasibility study for data center development in North West Nigeria (InfraCo). Covers data center design, ICT infrastructure and telecommunications integration.

title: China Eximbank and Credit Suisse AG provide $84 million syndicated buyer's credit facility for MTN Nigeria Communications to facilitate acquisition of telecommunication equipment from Huawei
description: In April 2017, China Eximbank and Credit Suisse AG signed an $84 million syndicated buyer's credit facility agreement with MTN Nigeria Communications Ltd. to facilitate its acquisition of telecommunication equipment from Huawei. This loan carries an interest rate of LIBOR plus a margin of 5.5%. The proceeds from the loan were used to finance 85% of the the value of a $106 million contract with Huawei. It is repayable in 8 equal installments beginning August 2018. The loan achieved a 100% disbursement rate.

title: INT Towers Nigeria \u2014 Equity Investment (Telecoms Tower Infrastructure)
description: BII invested $20M equity in INT Towers Limited in February 2015. INT Towers owns and operates over 9,100 telecoms towers across seven regions in Nigeria and is a wholly owned subsidiary of the IHS Towers Group. The investment enables mobile network operators to provide 2G/3G/4G connectivity to Nigerian consumers and businesses. Investment exited by September 2019.
recipient_organisation: INT Towers Limited (IHS Towers Nigeria subsidiary)

title: CPCIF Strategic Minority Stake in Venture Garden Nigeria \u2014 Fintech Platform
description: Convergence Partners Communications Infrastructure Fund (CPCIF) invested $20 million for a strategic minority stake in Venture Garden Nigeria (VGN), a diversified fintech holding company with significant operations in Nigeria. VGN provides innovative, data-driven, end-to-end technology platforms addressing reconciliation and payment processing inefficiencies across multiple industry verticals including financial services, education, aviation, power, downstream oil and gas, and cybersecurity. Investment was made at CPCIF final close (capital over $200 million). Venture Garden Group later incubated companies including Flutterwave, Helium Health, AppZone, and GreenHouse Capital.

title: IHS Nigeria Tower Expansion Loan (2015)
description: IFC provided a $50 million loan to IHS Nigeria Plc to finance the acquisition and upgrade of 2,705 towers from Etisalat Nigeria (now 9mobile) in a Buy and Lease Back (BLB) arrangement. IHS Nigeria is the largest tower company in Nigeria operating over 30,000 towers across the country. The investment enabled IHS to expand its portfolio significantly and provide 2G/3G/4G infrastructure to mobile network operators, supporting connectivity for millions of Nigerians.
